description: Composite figure group combining an atomic force microscopy (AFM) topography map (Fig. 7) with a nanoindentation load–displacement curve (Fig. 8). Panel (a) is a brown-to-dark-orange AFM height map of a surface containing a grain boundary, which appears as a dark elongated band running diagonally across the scan; no scale bar, height colour bar or labelled vertical axis is printed. Superimposed on the scan are three horizontal rows of marker symbols marking indentation positions: triangles (△, Line #1) and diamonds (◇, Line #2) in the two upper rows and open squares (□, Line #3) in the lower row, according to the inset legend. The horizontal axis is "Position (μm)" with printed ticks 0, 3, 6, 9, 12; the markers are spaced at roughly regular intervals along each line and span from about 1 μm to just under 12 μm. Panel (b) plots "Load P" against "Penetration h [nm]" (printed ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12; load ticks at 100 intervals up to 400): a jagged red loading trace rises monotonically to the ~400 level near h ≈ 10 nm, with a smooth black line drawn through it and no unloading branch. Together the panels show where the near-boundary indentations were placed and the shape of one representative loading curve (spherical tip, nominal R = 50 μm per the citing text).
measured_quantities: load P (unit glyph ambiguous; printed as '[∞N]')
AFM surface height (unlabelled colour scale, arbitrary units)

observations.observation: The figure group mixes two different modalities: an AFM topography map with overlaid indentation positions and a nanoindentation load–displacement curve.
Panel (a) renders surface height in a brown/orange-to-dark colour scale and shows a dark elongated band running diagonally across the scan, i.e. the region near the grain boundary.
An inset legend in panel (a) labels three marker sets: triangle = Line #1, diamond = Line #2, square = Line #3.

Indentation markers in panel (a) are arranged in three horizontal rows, with Line #1 and Line #2 in the upper two rows and Line #3 in the lower row; the two upper rows converge/overlap near Position ≈ 4-5 μm.
Panel (a) x-axis is labelled 'Position (μm)' with printed ticks at 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12; markers span from just right of the 0 tick to just left of the 12 tick.
Panel (a) carries no scale bar, no height colour bar and no labelled vertical axis, so the AFM scan size in nm is not obtainable from the image.
Panel (b) axes are 'Load P' with printed ticks 0, 100, 200, 300, 400 and 'Penetration h [nm]' with printed ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.

The measured curve in panel (b) is drawn in red and is strongly serrated (jagged), rising monotonically from the origin to about the 400 load level at h ≈ 10 nm, with a smooth black line drawn through the data.
Only a loading branch is visible in panel (b); no unloading/withdrawal segment is plotted.

The y-axis unit of panel (b) is rendered as '[∞N]' in the image, so the printed unit glyph itself is ambiguous (nanoindentation loads in such curves are conventionally μN, but the figure as supplied does not render it legibly).
The caption states Fig. 7 is an AFM image of the surface near the grain boundary together with the measurement points, and Fig. 8 is a load–displacement curve.

The citing text states that nanoindentation with a spherical tip was applied to measure mechanical properties near a grain, and that the measurement points lie along one of the three lines across the boundary.
The citing text states the plotted load–displacement curve was obtained with a nominal spherical tip radius R = 50 μm.

The citing text asserts that the elastic modulus near the boundary is smaller than in other regions, whose values are similar to each other but at a different level because the grains have different orientations; this modulus result is reported in a later figure (Fig. 9), not in the present panels.

subfigures.description: AFM topography (height) map of a surface near a grain boundary, rendered in brown/orange-to-dark tones with a dark diagonal band through the scan. Three horizontal rows of markers are overlaid: △ (Line #1) and ◇ (Line #2) in the upper two rows, □ (Line #3) in the lower row, as defined by an inset legend. X-axis is 'Position (μm)' with ticks 0, 3, 6, 9, 12; no vertical axis label, no scale bar and no height colour bar are present.

Nanoindentation load–displacement curve: 'Load P' (y, ticks 0-400 at 100 intervals; unit glyph rendered ambiguously, printed as '[∞N]') versus 'Penetration h [nm]' (x, ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12). A serrated/jagged red measured trace rises monotonically to about the 400 level at h ≈ 10 nm, with a smooth black line fitted through it; only the loading branch is shown.
